items.question: Composition versus inheritance in a .NET microservice?
items.answer: A worker or API host is a composition root: inject IMessageHandler, ICache, IClock. Inheritance is for genuine is-a specialization with a stable virtual surface. Deep domain hierarchies across service boundaries become versioning pain. C# still allows one base class; extra roles are interfaces.
followUps: When is an abstract base still the right call?
How do default interface methods change evolution?
items.sixtySeconds: Compose services. Inherit for shared polymorphic behavior with one base. Interfaces for extra capabilities.

items.question: virtual, override, abstract, sealed, and new — what does each do?
items.answer: virtual opens a slot. override replaces that slot in the derived type. abstract demands an override and forbids instantiating the type. sealed on a class blocks derivation; sealed override blocks further override. new hides a member and does not participate in the base slot — calling through the base type still hits the base method.
followUps: Show a bug caused by new instead of override.
Can you override a non-virtual method?
items.sixtySeconds: Dispatch uses the override slot. new is a different member. Interviewers listen for that sentence.

items.question: How do C# interfaces differ from TypeScript interfaces?
items.answer: A C# interface is a CLR contract: implementing types have metadata, default interface methods can run, and you can cast to the interface. TypeScript interfaces erase at compile time. Explicit interface implementation in C# hides the member unless you cast. DIM lets you add members without recompiling every implementer, with diamond-resolution rules.
followUps: Can a struct implement an interface? What happens?
What is an explicit implementation used for?
items.sixtySeconds: C# interfaces survive at runtime. TS interfaces do not. Boxing happens when a struct is cast to an interface.

items.question: Why use a record for an auth token or Redis DTO?
items.answer: Positional records give concise immutable-shaped data, value equality, and with-expressions for copies. Two AuthToken values with the same claims compare equal even if they are different objects — useful for tests and cache keys. record struct avoids a heap object when the payload is tiny. Hashing must stay consistent if you put them in dictionaries.
followUps: record versus record struct versus readonly struct?
items.sixtySeconds: Records: value equality and with. Redis/auth DTOs fit. Equality details are the next topic.

items.question: What breaks if Equals and GetHashCode disagree?
items.answer: Dictionary, HashSet, and many caches use the hash to bucket then Equals to confirm. If two objects compare equal but hash differently, lookups miss. If they hash equal but Equals is reference-based, you get duplicates. Mutable keys that change after insert vanish. Implement IEquatable<T> to avoid boxing value types.
followUps: How do records generate these methods?
Why is string a good dictionary key and a mutable DTO a bad one?
items.sixtySeconds: Hash and equals are a pair. Never mutate a key. IEquatable<T> for structs.
